answer: Require each new agent to lock a scarce token stake that is slashed if it double-signs or breaks a dispute-backed service commitment. Reputation and voting weight then accrue only to stake that survives real interactions, so minting a thousand names does not create a thousand trusted voices; the attacker must buy and risk a thousand independent stakes. This raises the cost from cheap account creation to costly capital at risk, whether the agents trade on mesa, sail an ocean marketplace, or compete at the zenith of demand.
